topic.title: Gold exchange before Dhanteras
topic.claim: After May's duty hike, old gold became a big part of jewellers' supply, and the exchange bonus is what it costs them to turn your locker into a sale.
topic.moment: The jeweller weighing mummy's old bangles before Dhanteras and offering an exchange bonus.

turn.believed: the exchange bonus is the jeweller doing you a favour
turn.actually: since imports fell after the duty hike, old gold is a main supply line, and exchange guarantees a sale

topic.because: the exchange bonus has always been a sales incentive; since the May duty hike jewellers lean far more on old gold, so you can't tell from the counter whether the bonus is a real deal
topic.payoff: If the exchange route isn't clearly cheaper than the cash route, it was never a bonus.

proof.fact: Customs duty on gold rose from 6% to 15% (BCD 5 to 10, AIDC 1 to 5) from 13 May 2026; gold imports fell about 70% after the hike
GTRI: effective duty on gold including IGST rose to 18.45% from 9.18%
46% of Kalyan Jewellers' revenue in Q1 FY27 was from recycled gold; nearly 65% of jewellery sales at Joy Alukkas are from old gold exchanges
India raised import duties on gold and silver to 15% from 6%
The import duty increased from 6% to 15%; exchange of old gold jewellery for new limited the price pass-through

paragraphs: This Dhanteras, the jeweller will offer an "exchange bonus" on mummy's old bangles. Since May, old gold is a big part of what he sells.
slides.why_swipe: 'supply line' contradicts the favour everyone assumes; what changed in May?

paragraphs: Mummy takes the red pouch from her wedding out of the almirah and puts the bangles on the glass counter.
He runs them through the karat machine, weighs them, knocks off a few percent for "melting loss", then smiles. "Aunty, exchange bonus bhi denge."
Mummy came home happy. I did the maths later and wasn't so sure.
slides.why_swipe: the reader has lived this scene; the narrator found something out

paragraphs: In May, the duty on imported gold went from 6% to 15%. Within a month, import volumes fell about 70%.
slides.why_swipe: imports collapsed; the gap is filled from somewhere

paragraphs: After the hike, more of the gold started coming from family lockers.
Kalyan says recycled gold was almost half its revenue in April to June, and more than half by June.
slides.why_swipe: the scale is proven; what does the jeweller get beyond the gold?

paragraphs: The exchange bonus isn't new. It has always been a way to close a sale.
What changed in May is how much of that sale now runs on your gold. The bonus might be a genuine deal, or it might come back to him on the new piece.
**You just can't tell which from the counter.**
slides.why_swipe: the seller's side is out; how do you tell if your bonus is real?

paragraphs: So get two numbers in writing, a few days before Dhanteras.
A: the new piece with the exchange, after the bonus. B: the new piece at full price, minus what another jeweller pays you in cash for the same bangles.
**If A isn't clearly lower than B, the bonus was just a fair price for mummy's gold, called a gift.**

draft.caption: Has anyone in your family ever asked for the cash price of their old gold before taking the exchange bonus?
draft.alt_text: A text carousel arguing that after the May 2026 gold duty hike, old gold exchange became a main supply for jewellers, with a test for whether an exchange bonus is real.

cover.headline: Mummy's old gold is now the jeweller's [supply line.]
cover.sub: Before you take the exchange bonus, check one thing.

end.save: Get the two numbers a few days before 6 Nov.
end.send: Send it to whoever in your family is exchanging gold this Dhanteras.
end.promise: The real price of things in India.

mechanism.broken_premise: None fails outright. The weakest link is the causal framing — that the May 2026 duty hike is *why* the bonus might be illusory. The post itself concedes (slide 5) that an exchange bonus was always potentially just fair metal value relabeled; the hike only raised jewellers' appetite for recycled gold, which could as easily push bonuses up (competition for scrap) as hollow them out. But this framing is presented as context, not as a load-bearing premise, so it doesn't break the take.
mechanism.actual_mechanism: In an Indian gold exchange, the jeweller assays your old piece (karat + weight), applies a melting/purity deduction, values the metal at the prevailing rate, and subtracts that from the new piece's price; you then pay the difference plus making charges, with 3% GST levied on the new piece either way. An 'exchange bonus' is only a genuine discount if it exceeds fair metal value — e.g. a making-charge waiver or a valuation above spot — rather than merely waiving the melting-loss deduction you'd otherwise lose. Because the metal value and the 'bonus' are bundled into one counter quote, the only way to isolate a real discount is the post's A-vs-B test: exchange-quote-after-bonus versus full-price-minus-independent-cash-valuation.
